Sentence (English): I bought this to replace my older model GE portable dishwasher that I bought used, and lasted for 10 years.
Comments (English): [ Best Portable Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I bought this to replace my older model GE portable dishwasher that I bought used, and lasted for 10 years. I can only hope this new one lasts as long. So far I have been thoroughly impressed with how well it cleans. I have used all the cleaning cycles and quite frankly, unless you really need to sterilze something, the normal wash cycle is all you really need. I am using pods detergent for the main cleaning cycle, and a small glob of gel for the pre-rinse cycle, and jet dry. My dishes and glasses have never been cleaner. Also, its as quiet as a modern under counter dishwasher. Very impressed. There is not a heated dry cycle, but I didn't use that on the previous dishwasher anyway. When the cycle completes, open the door, pull out the racks, and turn the ceiling fan on for a bit. Dries fairly quickly. As others have noted, the hose does not seat properly when retracted and sticks out a bit. Kind of annoying, but where I store it when not in use, the not fully retracted hose can't be seen anyway, so who cares. But GE should fix that on future models. My only real complaint is about the controls location. They are on the top of the door and not visible when in use. Not a big deal, but having a time remaining display that can't be seen while the dishwasher is in use is kind of pointless. My recommendation to GE is to cut off about two inches from the top surface, and the display will be visible while in use. I have only had this dishwasher for a month, so I can't yet speak to longevity, but my initial impression is very positive and I recommend.

Sentence (English): We bought this to replace a dishwasher that had quit washing properly.
Comments (English): We bought this to replace a dishwasher that had quit washing properly. We've never had an LG appliance previously, but after reading reviews, I thought it was a good model to go with. So far we've been pleased with its performance. Dishes go in without having been pre-washed and those dishes come out clean. Love the third rack at the top. Also love the options on the control panel, which surprisingly has not caused my wife to complain over its top location (a first for us). I don't understand the need for an app to control this dishwasher remotely - it's not like I'm going to start this thing while I'm at the ball game.

I'm very disappointed in the purchase overall and feel I wasted my money going for what I thought was the top of line.

Sentence (English): I've rarely a dishwasher most of my life and now only do 2 loads a week at most, so I may not be the best reviewer.
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher seems OK but Lowes installation was bad ] || ---------------- || I've rarely a dishwasher most of my life and now only do 2 loads a week at most, so I may not be the best reviewer. That said, this dishwas seems to do a pretty good so far, particularly for the on sale price I paid. However, the contractor Lowes sent to install the dishwasher is costing me most of the money I saved on the sales price of the dishwasher.The reason I bought the dishwasher was to save time and energy over handwashing. So, far the dishwasher seems to be doing that. I seem to be saving at least 2 hours a week. My energy bill seems lower, though this hard to tell, as I have a new furnace, too.As important, the dishwasher gets most of the dishes as clean as hand washing or cleaner,with minimal spotting of glassware even when I use Aldi detergent packs and no rinse product. There are a few things it doesn't clean well, e.g., sheets used for baking and glasses used for Metamucil or with dried coffee & cream, but most of these are quick and easy to hand wash.I can't say how reliable it is. Whirlpool long ago had a reputation for making ultra-reliable appliance, but over the last 20 years their reputation for reliability's been all over the place. I've had it only 1 month, but so far so good. So I may amend this review based on further use.It's looks good. Its also been easy to clean.Also it's quiet--not as quiet as a sibling's top of the line Bosch, but it's quiet enough so I can work in the next room with open door and not be bothered. I also paid about 55% less than what I would have paid for a Bosch similar to what my sibling has--if you don't count the money I have to spend to have the installation redone to fix the job the Lowes contract did.So far the dishwasher biggest negative, besides the problems I had with its installation, is the instructions in the owner's manual are abysmal. The instruction are difficutl to follow, poorly organized, and make almost no sense. I'm still trying to figure out all of the controls and option even though I've read the instruction over 10 times. Fortunately, the basic progam is easy to use, so I can use the dishwasher. The big problem I've had with the dishwasher has not with the dishwasher itself but with the local installer Lowes sent. It was a very bad experience. I paid Lowes $210.00 for delivery, haul away of any old dishwasher, and installation of the new one. There was no old dishwasher to haul away, and there was a bay ready with wiring, so installing it should have have been quick and easy job, but that wasn't the case. The contractor Lowes sent took far too long and did a poor job.I had to set aside an entire day as the installer wouldn't give a time they were coming to do work the work, just a day of the week. Then the installer didn't finish it that day and took a week to come back to finish it. I realized on closer inspection, several hours that after the contractor's minions left on the second day, the job was still unfinished. There were problems with how the dishwasher was placed and with the plumbing.The Lowes contractor installed the dishwasher so the counter edge covers almost all of the controls. I can't see or use most of the controls when the dishwasher's door is shut. I can only use the dishwasher because it's not in straight, so I can reach the "on" button. Also, the plumbing work they did is just terrible. I now have to pay someone else to have the installation fixed, blowing much, if not all, of the money I saved from the sale price--and taking up even more of my time.My advice is if you buy an appliance from Lowes, don't pay Lowes for a contractor to install the appliance. The contracor Lowes sent to install my dishwasher was bad. The contractor wouldn't say what time of day they were coming. Then they took far too long, turning a one day job into a two day job. And now I have to pay someone else to fix the work of the Lowes contractor. Despite the dishwasher so far working reasonably well and being very quiet, I'm still only giving the dishwaher a 3 out of 5 stars. It loses half star for the useless owner's manual. It loses a star and half the terrible installation. The installation was so bad, I'm tempted to take away 2.5 for the installation and give the dishwasher 2 stars or even 1 star, as installation is going to end up costing me 3 days and probably cost twice as much what Lowes said it would cost. While this rating may seem unfair to Whirlpool, I don't think it is. Whirlpool has enough clout to ensure that Lowes and other Whirlpool retailers employ contractors who can install Whirlpool appliances in a timely and correct manner.

Sentence (English): This is the most disappointing appliance I have ever owned.
Comments (English): [ Dish-appointing Appliance ] || ---------------- || This is the most disappointing appliance I have ever owned. We purchased Cafe appliances for our kitchen remodel 2 years ago. The bad: (1) The wheels on the bottom rack fall off constantly and are left to melt in the bottom of the machine. We have bought several replacement wheels and have to keep them on hand because the wheels come off so frequently. These wheels are extremely poorly designed. (2) The lid covering the area where you add drying agent is already coming off we open it - the knobs holding it together are showing wear and are poorly designed. (3) The metal spokes in the dish racks bend very easily and lose their shape. They seem likely to break in the future. (4) The dishes are never fully dry! You run a wash cycle and everything is still wet at the end. Very wet. I have to take most of the dishes out and dry them on the counter or by hand, which takes up time and space, and means that I cannot do dishes as efficiently. The ultra dry function helps a bit, but that function is not recommended for use on certain types of flooring - it can damage wood/laminate. Just an overall miserable appliance that is pretty but not very functional for everyday living. I do not recommend this product.

Sentence (English): This is the second Bosch dishwasher to faithfully serve my family.
Comments (English): [ Just As I Expected! ] || ---------------- || This is the second Bosch dishwasher to faithfully serve my family. The first one, still operating just fine I must add, was 9 years old and had lived through those nine years of boisterous gatherings, parties, and multiple daily washings without incident. The dishes always came out clean, and dry (! ) and the machine itself was oh! so quiet the whole time. I love that about Bosch dishwashers. One doesn't even know they are doing their dirty work when they're doing it. So when the door of my machine suddenly banged down--boom! --when I opened it one morning, I dreaded the idea that after 9 years of honoroable and exceptional service, it was dying. The washings were still as perfect as ever. But the door's serpentine belt which allowed one to gently lower the door open, I believe it was, had clearly failed. I knew a service call might be costly and after weighing the options, decided it was time to purchase a new one. Nine years! Oh my…As I have two dishwashers in my kitchen (we like to party here but nobody likes washing dishes), I considered swapping places with the other (unnamed brand, used as a backup) dishwasher with the older Bosch and buying a new one to replace it. But I didn't. I just bought one. And I love it. True to form, it does an excellent job, and this one even has a pull out rack at the top for those rubber spatulas and oddities one uses cooking and nobody seems to know where to place in a dishwasher. I love the sleek look to the new Bosch, too—fits right in to my white cabinet decor. Recently, I had an 'overflow' of dishes, so I had to use the other unnamed brand. I was immediately reminded how quiet the Bosch is. I mean, this other brand is absolutely obnoxious. I couldn't even hear the TV in the next room with it running. The Bosh? One doesn't even know it's running.I'm thinking about getting another Bosch. The unnamed cheaper brand really looks dated, and is noisy--very noisy! The new Bosch dishwasher is so quiet I have to check to see if it's still running even when I'm standing right in front of it! It has a light at the base which reflects off the floor, so it is easy to see when it's running. And the door pops open when it's done to help speed the drying. No questions about whether or not the dishes are done.Well, just what I expected. I've talked myself into a second new Bosch dishwasher! I do love my Bosch.

Sentence (English): This is the second Bosch dishwasher to faithfully serve my family.
Comments (English): [ Just As I Expected! ] || ---------------- || This is the second Bosch dishwasher to faithfully serve my family. The first one, still operating just fine I must add, was 9 years old and had lived through those nine years of boisterous gatherings, parties, and multiple daily washings without incident. The dishes always came out clean, and dry (! ) and the machine itself was oh! so quiet the whole time. I love that about Bosch dishwashers. One doesn't even know they are doing their dirty work when they're doing it. So when the door of my machine suddenly banged down--boom! --when I opened it one morning, I dreaded the idea that after 9 years of honoroable and exceptional service, it was dying. The washings were still as perfect as ever. But the door's serpentine belt which allowed one to gently lower the door open, I believe it was, had clearly failed. I knew a service call might be costly and after weighing the options, decided it was time to purchase a new one. Nine years! Oh my… As I have two dishwashers in my kitchen (we like to party here but nobody likes washing dishes), I considered swapping places with the other (unnamed brand, used as a backup) dishwasher with the older Bosch and buying a new one to replace it. But I didn't. I just bought one. And I love it. True to form, it does an excellent job, and this one even has a pull out rack at the top for those rubber spatulas and oddities one uses cooking and nobody seems to know where to place in a dishwasher. I love the sleek look to the new Bosch, too—fits right in to my white cabinet decor. Recently, I had an 'overflow' of dishes, so I had to use the other unnamed brand. I was immediately reminded how quiet the Bosch is. I mean, this other brand is absolutely obnoxious. I couldn't even hear the TV in the next room with it running. The Bosh? One doesn't even know it's running. I'm thinking about getting another Bosch. The unnamed cheaper brand really looks dated, and is noisy--very noisy! The new Bosch dishwasher is so quiet I have to check to see if it's still running even when I'm standing right in front of it! It has a light at the base which reflects off the floor, so it is easy to see when it's running. And the door pops open when it's done to help speed the drying. No questions about whether or not the dishes are done. Well, just what I expected. I've talked myself into a second new Bosch dishwasher! I do love my Bosch.

Sentence (English): I've only had this dishwasher for a week, but there are few things that are clear.
Comments (English): [ Clean Dishes - Absolutely Hate App Delay Start ] || ---------------- || I've only had this dishwasher for a week, but there are few things that are clear. It's super quiet, it looks great and the dishes are clean. All good and expected of a dishwasher espeically for the price. I splurged on this appliance for the Bosch name. It's my first Bosh but for me at the end of the day it's still just a dishwasher. The reason that I'm taking away 3 stars is because this appliance does not have a delay start button on the panel. I must download and install an app on my phone to do delay start. This is Totally Unacceptable at this price point and I'm Really Disappointed. I just want to press the remote start and be done, but now I have to connect my dishwasher to wifi. NO. , I shouldn't have to do that. If you want to provide that option to have an app then do so, but also give me a delay start button on the dishwasher itself. I tried pairing the app to device and after 10 mins gave up. That's 10 mins of my life that I can't get back. No parts of life should involve downloading and installing an app to start a load of dishes. I tried pairing the next day and finally got it to work. The good thing about the app is that I'm suppose to be able to set it so that my dishwasher runs everynight, so I do like that capability. if it worked. Appearntly I still have to spend more time to figure this out as I set the schedule, but the next day, my dishes are still sitting there dirty. So, I've opted to just start it before going to bed until I can figure out delay start. I'll likely need to call in for support which I wouldn't have to do if I just had a delay start button. Had I known that it didn't have delay start, I wouldn't have purchased it.

Sentence (English): After several months, I regret this purchase because of the horrible racks, especially the middle one.
Comments (English): [ Horrible racks ] || ---------------- || After several months, I regret this purchase because of the horrible racks, especially the middle one. They are frustrating and inefficient. It seems the middle rack tries to tip dishes to force water to run off. This is ineffective and, at the same time, makes many things not fit properly in the rack. The fold down shelves are thick and prevent many glasses from being loaded. Wine glasses fall over. Plastic containers are particularly frustrating, both not fitting in the spaces and, also, flipping over and filling with water. In the lower rack, plates are fine, but the the two rows of tines are too close side-to-side to allow multiple bowls to be loaded. The idea of having a utensils shelf does not really give extra room for plates and bowls because a big gap was left in the lower rack to receive a utensils basket, just in case someone wants one. For me that is wasted space.The utensils shelf sort of works, but I find it slower to load and unload than a traditional basket and, as mentioned, it hasn't saved space.Overall, I must run the machine once a day and occasionally twice, but my old machine only had to run once every day and a half. This is because of the poor racks. This also means that the energy efficiency numbers are misleading because the machine must be run more often.Finally, the noise level (SPL) depends upon which cycle is run. Auto, the suggested cycle, is noiser than normal. Using a Niosh SPL meter app on my iPhone with the built in mic, this machine is not as much of a sound savings relative to my old machine as I hoped for. I looked for Bosch's definitions for the SPL claims (distance of measurment, etc.), and am guessing they are not reporting peak noise levels or typical noise levels, but some sort of average, including silent rest periods. That is just a guess on my part and I wish they published their definitions.

Sentence (English): I first bought this model of diswasher in 2008, in bright red, which suited my kitchen.
Comments (English): [ Repeat purchase ] || ---------------- || I first bought this model of diswasher in 2008, in bright red, which suited my kitchen. That lasted until 2021. I think it was the wash arm that was the problem and could have probably been repaired, but it was showing its age and I had the money, so I opted to replace it with the newer version, as it has more features and was more efficient. I'm pleased that it gives the same excellent trouble-free performance wash after wash as my original one did. I was sad to see that Bosch had limited the range to just 'white' finishes and breifely considered going with another brand which had a red model, but in the end i stuck with Bosch. They were considerably more expensive, but having owned the red model for 13 triuble free years, i knew that the buold quality and performance were excellent and ultimately that is way more important than the colour of the machine. The one thing i didn't like was the new fitment on the hose. I understand it is supposed to stop leaks, but it wasn't clear when i bought it that it wouldn't fit through the hole on my countertop. For various reasons i couldn't make the hole larger, or drill another, so i had to splash out another £48 on a connecting hose so that i could get it plumbed in. This was a very poor design choice from Bosch and I felt it was a little underhand not to make it very clear that the product had changed significantly, or to have designed it so that the hose wouldn't fit a standard countertop 'hose hole'. That is my only gripe and, having had the machine for a couple of years, i had forgotten about it until being prompted to write a review reminded me. Bosch, take note of what people remember when you make design changes to your products!

Comments (English): [ Shinsegae was not a department store, it was a dishwasher. ] || ---------------- || I purchased this about six months ago when it appeared on Gold Box. Unfortunately, installation wasn't possible because my kitchen sink was too small. However, after moving recently, I bought it immediately without hesitation. It is the dishwasher I had been dreaming of, having seen countless glowing reviews. We have been married for seven years, and the cause and trigger of our arguments has always been washing dishes. My husband considers washing dishes a huge chore, and we used to fight over who had to do everything after we cooked the meal. It hasn't even been a week since we bought the dishwasher, but I think this will likely be the best purchase I’ve made this year (or maybe even the best purchase of my entire life). You might wonder why we need a 6-person capacity when there are only two of us, but when we have dinner, pots and pans are a given. Even the 6-person model is packed tight. I reorganized the dish drying rack immediately after bringing the dishwasher in. Even though it takes up a lot of space, the sheer size and whiteness itself serve as an interior design element. — By the way, the rice grains on the spatula facing the door didn't fall off, but that is a problem that can be solved by simply moving it to the back. I want to use this for a lifetime, so before putting the dishwasher in... I rinse the rice grains and food residue with water first. The strainer for food residue isn't detachable, but if you scrub it with a straw brush, even small debris gets cleaned out. Satisfied, very satisfied, super-super satisfied.

Now that I'm in my third year of living alone, washing dishes has become such a hassle that I've lost the desire to cook. At first, I used too little detergent and didn't add fabric softener, so the dishes came out a bit messy. Sentence (English): After several months, I regret this purchase because of the horrible racks, especially the middle one.
Comments (English): [ Horrible racks ] || ---------------- || After several months, I regret this purchase because of the horrible racks, especially the middle one. They are frustrating and inefficient. It seems the middle rack tries to tip dishes to force water to run off. This is ineffective and, at the same time, makes many things not fit properly in the rack. The fold down shelves are thick and prevent many glasses from being loaded. Wine glasses fall over. Plastic containers are particularly frustrating, both not fitting in the spaces and, also, flipping over and filling with water. In the lower rack, plates are fine, but the the two rows of tines are too close side-to-side to allow multiple bowls to be loaded. The idea of having a utensils shelf does not really give extra room for plates and bowls because a big gap was left in the lower rack to receive a utensils basket, just in case someone wants one. For me that is wasted space. The utensils shelf sort of works, but I find it slower to load and unload than a traditional basket and, as mentioned, it hasn't saved space. Overall, I must run the machine once a day and occasionally twice, but my old machine only had to run once every day and a half. This is because of the poor racks. This also means that the energy efficiency numbers are misleading because the machine must be run more often. Finally, the noise level (SPL) depends upon which cycle is run. Auto, the suggested cycle, is noiser than normal. Using a Niosh SPL meter app on my iPhone with the built in mic, this machine is not as much of a sound savings relative to my old machine as I hoped for. I looked for Bosch's definitions for the SPL claims (distance of measurment, etc.), and am guessing they are not reporting peak noise levels or typical noise levels, but some sort of average, including silent rest periods. That is just a guess on my part and I wish they published their definitions.

Sentence (English): I decided to buy the dishwasher because of its good reviews.
Comments (English): [ Defective dishwashers - They are not responsible. ] || ---------------- || I decided to buy the dishwasher because of its good reviews. Everything is nice until you run into a problem that becomes "your word against theirs." When removing the baskets in order to carry out the first cleaning of the device (after the first weeks), I realize that the rubber gasket that runs along the entire perimeter of the tank is cracked, deformed and, in some parts, detached. I contact the technical service, which sends someone to take a photograph and the factory response after the check is that "it is not covered by warranty" and they allege that I have used a detergent or "substance" not recommended for the apparatus. Well, they are not right, from day one top brand detergent has been used (no private label) and much less another "substance" has been used for washing. I will contact technical support again to find a solution and will modify the review accordingly.
Comments (Original): [ Lavajillas con defecto - No se hacen responsables. ] || ---------------- || Decidí comprar el lavavajillas por sus buenas críticas. Todo es bonito hasta que te encuentras con un problema que se convierte en 'tu palabra contra la suya'.Al extraer las cestas con tal de realizar la primera limpieza del aparato (pasadas las primeras semanas), me doy cuenta de que la junta de goma que recorre todo el perímetro de la cuba se encuentra agrietada, deformada y, en algunas partes, desprendida.Me pongo en contacto con el servicio técnico, el cual envía a alguien para realizar alguna fotografía y la respuesta de fábrica después del chequeo es que 'no entra en garantía' y alegan a que habré utilizado un detergente o 'substancia' no recomendable para el aparato.Bueno, pues no están en lo cierto, desde el primer día se ha usado detergente de primera marca (nada de marca blanca) y mucho menos se ha empleado otra 'substancia' para el lavado.Voy a volver a ponerme en contacto con el servicio técnico con tal de buscar una solución y modificaré la reseña acorde.

After a formal letter through OCU, they still cannot locate the problem, since they claim that "we are not aware of any manufacturing defect in the door seal of the appliance", when I stressed from the beginning (and as can be seen in the photos) that the problem is in the seals inside the tub and not in the door seals (which are perfectly fine). Edit: They still do not take responsibility for the defect. They assume from a couple of photos taken by the technician that the defect is due to misuse on my part. I am very afraid that if you do not contract their premium warranty service, any defect that the appliance has will be alleged as misuse. I decided to buy the dishwasher because of its good reviews. Everything is nice until you encounter a problem that becomes "your word against theirs". When I removed the baskets to clean the appliance for the first time (after the first few weeks), I noticed that the rubber seal that runs around the entire perimeter of the tub was cracked, deformed and, in some parts, detached. I contacted the technical service, which sent someone to take some photographs and the factory's response after the check was that "it is not covered by the guarantee" and they claim that I had used a detergent or "substance" not recommended for the appliance. Well, they are not right, from the first day a top brand detergent was used (no white label) and much less any other "substance" was used for washing. I am going to contact the technical service again in order to find a solution and I will modify the review accordingly.

Asumen por un par de fotos realizadas por el técnico que el defecto se debe a un mal uso por mi parte.Mucho me temo que si no contratas su servicio de garantía premium, todo aquel defecto que tenga el aparato va a ser alegado como mal uso.Decidí comprar el lavavajillas por sus buenas críticas. Sentence (English): Big brands are big brands after all.
Comments (English): Big brands are big brands after all. This Panasonic dishwasher has a powerful dishwashing function. The key is that the dishes are washed very clean and it looks good. It has a total of three rotating spray arms, plus a set of spray perforations fixed on the inner wall of the dishwasher, for almost 360-degree cleaning without any dead ends. When working, you can obviously hear the powerful sound of water spraying inside. After cleaning, it has a hot air drying function to speed up the drying time. Of course, when the weather is dry, you can also choose to simply air dry to save electricity bills. After washing and drying the tableware, I can use it directly without sanitizing it again. The product description states that it can wash 5 sets of bowls, but I tried it and found that if there are no cups and plates, the number of spinners can actually reach more than twenty. For details, please refer to the product instruction manual. The installation master also responded quickly and came to help me install it.

Sentence (English): I've had this unit now since early December 2023.
Comments (English): I've had this unit now since early December 2023. As a dishwasher, it's been great. I'd say it does a better job than my old unit. Downsides are: * It doesn't fit as many dishes just due to the layout of the racks, so I have to run it more often. Not great, especially in a drought-ridden area where we're always looking for ways to use less water. It's likely that even though the unit uses less power, that's more than offset by the need to use it more often. * The app is pretty much required. I had hoped it wouldn't be. But if I want to set up a run delay or use some of the other less general features, I have to use the app. It's not great. I should be able to load up my unit, select the settings while I'm there and set it to go. I shouldn't need my phone. What happens when they decide not to maintain it anymore? I'll be locked out of features. * It's pretty quiet, but I'd expected that I wouldn't be able to hear it at all, like my last Bosch. But I can hear it a room away while watching television (hence the need for the delay feature, only accessible via the app)

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher because my Bosch had a problem with a water sensor, and the repair person suggested getting a new unit because one was a little older.
Comments (English): [ Quiet, but the layout is not my favorite. ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher because my Bosch had a problem with a water sensor, and the repair person suggested getting a new unit because one was a little older. However, I didn't analyze the Kitchenaid layout thoroughly before purchasing, and I am finding that I am disappointed. On the positive side, this unit is Extremely quiet! My downgrade in the rating is because of the arrangement of the tines, mainly on the bottom rack. My Bosch accomodated 12 plates, 7-8 smaller (shallow) bowls, and 5-6 large shallow bowls. The spacing between the tines varied - closer for plates, wider for bowls. Now I'm discovering that with the Kitchenaid, all the tines are aligned. The slightly deeper bowls won't fit and stand straight between the rows - there is not sufficient space - so I either need to lean them against the silver basket or hand wash. It also only holds 10 plates and 10 bowls. The Flex rack on top is good for coffee cups and three 6” diameter round bowls, but that's not what I use as much. The silverware basket has slots to keep the pieces separated, which is good for cleaning, but you need to grab them from the tops, so not as sanitary. Not a big deal, but I preferred the top, sideways slotted rack on the Bosch. It's not a bad dishwasher! Just depends on what you're looking for and what your needs are. Hopefully this will help someone in determining what works best for their situation.

Sentence (English): We have been looking for a long time for a new dishwasher and this product got great reviews.
Comments (English): [ Overall happy ] || ---------------- || We have been looking for a long time for a new dishwasher and this product got great reviews. Overall I am happy with how well it cleans and how much it can hold. However I do not think it is easy to use. We love having a delay feature on our dishwashers because we run it at night when everyone is sleeping. Unfortunately, this feature can only be used by logging on to the app each time. We have called customer support about this issue and watched reviews and got nowhere with this feature. I appreciate having an app to help customize but the "my schedule time" doesn't link with the "favorite" feature. I don't think with such a sophisticated system I should have to open an app and program my time to start every night. It's a pain and I'm reminded every time I use it how frustrating it is not to have a delay feature on the dishwasher. Would I buy again. probably not this model unless they fixed this problem.

Sentence (English): After doing a lot of research especially on Consumer Reports, I decided to purchase this model.

Sentence (English): I was surprised by how quiet it is and how excellent it is at washing dishes in all the programs I have used.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher because my Bosch had a problem with a water sensor, and the repair person suggested getting a new unit because one was a little older.
Comments (English): [ Quiet, but the layout is not my favorite. ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher because my Bosch had a problem with a water sensor, and the repair person suggested getting a new unit because one was a little older. However, I didn't analyze the Kitchenaid layout thoroughly before purchasing, and I am finding that I am disappointed. On the positive side, this unit is Extremely quiet! My downgrade in the rating is because of the arrangement of the tines, mainly on the bottom rack. My Bosch accomodated 12 plates, 7-8 smaller (shallow) bowls, and 5-6 large shallow bowls. The spacing between the tines varied - closer for plates, wider for bowls. Now I'm discovering that with the Kitchenaid, all the tines are aligned. The slightly deeper bowls won't fit and stand straight between the rows - there is not sufficient space - so I either need to lean them against the silver basket or hand wash. It also only holds 10 plates and 10 bowls. The Flex rack on top is good for coffee cups and three 6" diameter round bowls, but that's not what I use as much. The silverware basket has slots to keep the pieces separated, which is good for cleaning, but you need to grab them from the tops, so not as sanitary. Not a big deal, but I preferred the top, sideways slotted rack on the Bosch. It's not a bad dishwasher! Just depends on what you're looking for and what your needs are. Hopefully this will help someone in determining what works best for their situation.

Sentence (English): The Home Depot ordering, delivery, & install was great.
Comments (English): The Home Depot ordering, delivery, & install was great. The unit is super quiet, the most sound occurs when it drains. Otherwise just a barely discernable hum now & then. It cleans really well however there is no easy way to tell when rinse aid is needed except the light on the door which is too late plus the racks have been challenging to figure out how to load most efficiently. It does not seem to hold nearly as many items as our 2004 Bosch it replaced. The fact we had to seek out, download & print off the owners manual was irritating too as there is a lot to learn about this generation of DW & we do not want to try to do all of that on our phone screen! Overall, we would buy again

Sentence (English): I am very disappointed in this dishwasher.
Comments (English): I am very disappointed in this dishwasher. I thought that Bosch was a good quality brand. I have had a Bosch dishwasher in the past and liked it. However, with this one the tines in the rack are too close together and it's hard to load the dishwasher so the dishes get clean. I end up having to wash several dishes after they have been run through the dishwasher. It also doesn't fit nearly as many dishes as the last dishwasher that I had and it is not nearly as quiet as it should be. I am also frustrated that to access some of the basic features like delay start, you have to download an app to use that function. I do not recommend purchasing this model.

I've been a loyal Kitchenaid customer for 10 years and purchased a new dishwasher for $1100 in 2020. The installation process was challenging – the water inlet valve was cross-threaded at the factory, leading to a return and replacement (install #2).Within a year, I received a recall notice from Kitchenaid regarding the pumps. Despite attempts, scheduling a service person was difficult, so they sent me a brand new dishwasher as a replacement. I installed the replacement myself (install #3). Unfortunately, within a year, issues with the control board and pump arose. Lowes' extended warranty covered replacements, but they cautioned about the declining quality of Kitchenaid products.Six months later, the new board failed again, followed by another pump failure. Lowes decided to issue a full refund of $1100 for the dishwasher. I used that refund to purchase a Bosch 800 series dishwasher. Interestingly, the Kitchenaid dishwasher that was once $1100 is now selling for $700 at Lowes. This experience has led me to the conclusion that Kitchenaid's quality has significantly declined, and I would not consider buying another Kitchenaid dishwasher.

Sentence (English): I've had this dishwasher for less than a month so have run it only a few times.
Comments (English): [ So far, so good ] || ---------------- || I've had this dishwasher for less than a month so have run it only a few times. Mostly I live alone, so need to use it only once or twice a week because I always wait until it's full. That means food gets dried on because pre-rinsing is discouraged. It's always a pleasant surprise that everything comes out sparkling clean, even on the normal setting. When the grandkids are here for a weekend, it gets run more often with bulkier loads, and even then it performs perfectly. I love the third rack for flatware and the fact that the lightweight door can be propped open part way. The Bosch uses half the detergent that my previous dishwasher did, and is amazingly quiet. That's important, because cycles are twice as long as the old one. My only quible is that the racks feel a little rickety when rolling them in and out; seems they should work more smoothly. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this machine and hope for many productive years from it.

It was obvious this dishwasher had been damaged somewhere between the manufacturer and our home. We returned this dishwasher and bought another Whirlpool but different model. We were so outdone when this model after unboxing also had damage with a dented front door. This one was returned to the store also and then we purchased a Bosch dishwasher. I think it is time for Whirlpool to take a serious look at the packaging of their products and do a better job. That was the first thing we noticed about how much better the Bosch packaging is in how heavy duty styrofoam was protecting all corners; the top was protected by thick wooden slats braced between the styrofoam on the top, front, and back sides. The time without a dishwasher along with time spent in purchasing and returning 2 dishwashers and paying for installations was most inconvenient and costly. We have had mostly Whirlpool appliances in our home so it is very disappointing to see the lack of quality in your current manufacturing process.

If you have a crappy dishwasher like I did, treat yourself and go for the upgrade! For me it's been worth every cent to make a boring daily task a little more streamlined, and with no need to dry those little pools of water that get caught in the feet of your coffee cups. The power of steam, yeah baby!

Sentence (English): I went in to purchase a new dishwasher that wouldn't breakdown in 2 years and after a TON of research I was dead set on purchasing the Bosch 800 Series.
Comments (English): I went in to purchase a new dishwasher that wouldn't breakdown in 2 years and after a TON of research I was dead set on purchasing the Bosch 800 Series. We were greeted quickly by a very nice gentleman and I told him exactly what I wanted and why I wanted that brand and style. They happened to have one on the floor (exact one I wanted, wrong color) and had my husband and I look it over. I loved it! But then he flipped the script on me! LOL He asked that before I purchased that one, to just look at the KitchenAid FreeFlex. (Bad idea! ) He explained the pro's and con's to both machines as well (and I knew he wasn't lying because again, I did a TON of research). Now I was torn! He told us that he simply wanted us to get the best machine to fit our needs and to think on it and research more if needed then either stop back in or order online. Well, after a couple days we decided to go with the FreeFlex and have yet to be disappointed! the 3rd rack is SO much sturdier with more adjustment options than the Bosch. It is beyond quiet, as in we can't even hear it running! The cycles do run a bit longer but I am fine with that. We got the recessed handle one and we love the sleek exterior look of it. And I definitely can't forget to mention the steel interior and tub. It does what a dishwasher should but most don't; it actually cleans my dishes WITHOUT pre-rinsing them! So far, I'd highly recommend this machine.Now, the not-so-good; The installation. We paid for it since we didn't want the headache of doing it. Well, here is how that went: Overall the install went ok but the guy said he needed to go get a different piece to plug the dishwasher into, then that piece would be plugged into the wall, which is fine. However, I'm not exactly sure WHERE he needed to go to get it or if he had to manufacture the piece himself but it took him 4 HOURS to return with the piece! it was extremely annoying, irritating, and quite frankly disrespectful of our time. This whole adventure started at approx. 10:45 am, he left at 12:35 pm to go get the piece, and finally returned at about 4:15 pm to finish the install and that was only after my Father-in-Law texted him to see where he was at, if he was coming back, or what was going on. Not impressed with this install at all.

This dishwasher is an absolute piece of garbage. The dishes come out dirty, even though I wash them with soap and a sponge before loading. Also, sometimes the soap doesn't even leave the dispenser and it is liquid soap, not a pod. The dispenser will pop open but the soap does not leave the reservoir. I have to run the dishwasher again wasting more energy. It always has this horrible chemical smell since the time that it was installed which transfers onto my dishes and cutlery. The third rack is a complete utter joke. The holes are large, so things fall through them, and there is nothing to hold things in place so everything kind of just flys around up there. spend a few hundred more and get a good quality dishwasher or you will be very dissatisfied with this one.

Sentence (English): I ordered the dishwasher in November and got a message from Costco with an early December delivery date.
Comments (English): [ Delivery logistics nightmare ] || ---------------- || I ordered the dishwasher in November and got a message from Costco with an early December delivery date. The installer then gave me 1/22 as the soonest available date. I called Costco to see if this was correct, no other installers? Meanwhile I'm getting emails from Costco saying I hadn't set up delivery. Costco comes back with an earlier date, which comes and goes, they made a mistake. Ok. Still more emails about me not having set up delivery. Now they are threatening to send the dishwasher back if I don't accept delivery soon. I check again, get told it's ok. Finally I get called by installer confirming 1/22 for delivery. Costco sends email, it's on its way! Then I get an email that the delivery was cancelled and the dishwasher was returned, on the day of the delivery. What? I called Costco, eventually got a return call. They don't know what's going on. The installer shows up with the dishwasher and installs it as Costco calls back canceling the return. I have never had an appliance delivery take so long, with so much miscommunication, and such poor customer service. Costco, you do so much right, it's mind boggling to see you do appliance delivery so poorly. The machine is okay. Not as good a quality as I'd hoped. That's what I get for buying on line and not seeing it in person. Several lessons learned.
